name: w5
responses: Automated retaliation risks rapid escalation, miscalculation, and attacks based on incomplete or misleading attribution. Even if a cyberattack on critical infrastructure is confirmed, a human decision-maker should assess proportionality, likely consequences, and whether nonmilitary responses could be more effective. Defensive automation can help contain damage, but initiating retaliation should remain under meaningful human control.

Automated retaliation risks escalating a crisis based on incomplete attribution, false positives, or misinterpreted signals. Cyber incidents can be routed through third-party systems or deliberately disguised, making “confirmed” attacks difficult to assess with certainty. A human decision process allows leaders to weigh proportionality, diplomatic alternatives, civilian consequences, and the risk of triggering broader conflict before authorizing any response. Automated defensive measures may be appropriate, but retaliatory force should remain under accountable human control.
